newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes down on oil demand.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes down on oil demand.

text.p: *Peso average remains at 26.347 to the dollar
Continued high demand for dollars by oil companies pulled down the Philippine peso at the close to 26.347 against the dollar on Wednesday from 26.345, dealers said.
Market volume thinned to $119.70 million from $136.50 million.
Oil companies will be buying $37 million on Thursday. They just purchased $38 million today at an average of 26.3475, dealers said. "Banks have been holding back on selling their dollars," one said.
Oil companies have increased their dollar purchases because of the removal of the foreign exchange cover for their oil imports since the industry was deregulated on February 8.
The peso, however, hit a day-low of 26.349 at midession before the sales of the oil companies. After the oil companies' requirements were easily met, the peso strenghtened, traders said.
Traders said the peso will not likely fall beyond 26.35 since the Central Bank is willing to sell dollars at 26.35.
